A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WorldSense research work. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and the tables, figures, and relocated failure-case material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 reports original WorldSense model evaluations, modality ablations, prompt-sensitivity results, and manually reviewed error analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and reports additional model evaluations in Table 2.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction, annotation and verification procedures, input configurations, and answer-matching evaluation remain unchanged. The added models are evaluated comparators, not changes to a proposed model or algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same WorldSense coverage: 1,662 videos, 3,172 QA pairs, eight domains, 67 subcategories, and 26 tasks, sourced from FineVideo and Music-AVQA. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added.

E2.justification: Table 2 substantially updates the comparison with video-SALMONN 2+ at 7B and 72B, Qwen3-Omni, Gemini 2.5 Flash, and Gemini 2.5 Pro. These introduce stronger open audio-visual and proprietary comparators while retaining every v2 participant.

E3.justification: The added video-SALMONN 2+ evaluations include 7B and 72B configurations, extending the explicitly reported open-model sizes beyond v2's 1B–8B range. The accuracy metric, dataset usage, prompts, and stated preprocessing procedures for retained evaluations are unchanged.

E4.justification: The modality ablations, task/audio breakdowns, 130-sample Gemini 1.5 Pro error analysis, and Appendix D prompt-sensitivity experiment are retained. Figure 8 and its two failure cases move from the appendix into Section 4.3; they are not new analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report point accuracies without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The unchanged random sampling of failure cases is an error-analysis procedure, not added uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds averages of 50.9% and 56.5% for video-SALMONN 2+ 7B/72B, 54.0% for Qwen3-Omni, and 52.3%/65.1% for Gemini 2.5 Flash/Pro, plus domain scores. Existing rows retain their values; the higher frontier comes from additional models. Section 4.2 also changes the stated video-only maximum from 40.2% to 54.0%, contradicting the unchanged 40.2% maximum in that table group.

T1.justification: Neither version introduces formal theorems, proofs, or mathematical derivations. The benchmark taxonomy and evaluation definitions remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction update the headline best accuracy from 48.0% to 65.1%, with Gemini 2.5 Pro replacing Gemini 1.5 Pro as the leading model. The introduction also replaces the Gemini-specific 15% modality-drop statement with a general decline claim. Benchmark novelty, scope, and principal contributions remain the same.

C2.justification: The explanations involving weak audio understanding, limited cross-modal integration, and reasoning failures are retained, as is the multiple-choice format limitation. The relocated failure-case discussion is lightly shortened without changing its substantive interpretation.

D1.justification: Implementation and access disclosures remain unchanged, including official model pipelines, 16-frame sampling for GPT 4o and Claude, Gemini 1.5 Pro raw-video uploads, A100 hardware, prompt templates, and dataset distribution/licensing information. No model-specific execution instructions accompany the added comparisons.

R1.justification: Five works are added: Gemini 2.5, video-SALMONN 2, Qwen3-Omni, DeepEyes, and DeepEyesV2. The first three support new evaluated comparators; DeepEyes and DeepEyesV2 extend the related-work citations. The existing benchmark positioning and novelty argument remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized wording updates and integrates the former Appendix E failure-case discussion into Section 4.3, subsequently relabeling the remaining appendices. Most prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: Table 2 expands to accommodate five additional model rows, and Figure 8 moves from the appendix to the main text. The figure assets themselves are unchanged; remaining differences largely involve text flow and pagination.

improvement.justification: The newer open and proprietary comparators make Table 2 more useful for assessing benchmark difficulty and model capabilities, providing a modest benefit over v2's narrower comparison. This benefit is tempered by incomplete narrative reconciliation: v3 incorrectly reports a 54.0% video-only maximum, and retains near-chance characterizations despite its stronger audio-visual results.
